The Team:

We are Datadog's in-house product experts. The technical solutions team enables Datadog's worldwide growth by educating potential clients and ensuring that existing customers are happy and successful. We share our technical and product expertise with customers through demos, presentations, technical evaluations, and ongoing support. Technical solutions is a growing global team that collaborates constantly to share knowledge and continuously advance our technical skillset.

The Opportunity:

The Partner Solution Architect (PSA) is a Datadog expert who will work closely with Datadog’s Director, Adoption Services, and is aligned to our Channels & Alliances business segment. The PSA is responsible for supporting a variety of technical initiatives and activities for our partners (for example: cloud migration, application modernization, DevOps transformation). They are accountable for the outcome of these initiatives, and frequently collaborate with both Datadog and Partner resources to drive success. The PSA is a trusted technical advisor for our Partner channel.

You Will:

  • Ensure the successful onboarding, training, enablement, and certification of partner technical resources;
  • Participate in periodic joint business planning and review sessions to ensure direct alignment between Datadog and Partner technical teams;
  • Collaborate internally to support Partner technical initiatives such as end-customer demonstrations and proofs of value; partner team enablement workshops; assessment, advice, and coaching on lead practices;
  • Advocate on behalf of Partners’ technical concerns (use cases, feature requests, support issues, e.g.) with Datadog internal teams and personnel, helping to bring those concerns to resolution;
  • Analyze and understand Partner service offerings on a regular basis and provide recommendations to enhance the value of those services through greater or improved adoption of Datadog features and capabilities;
  • Collaborate with Datadog’s product management, engineering and technical services teams to help identify and prioritize new features and capabilities;
  • Continuously help curate and evolve lead/best practices for Datadog platform adoption and success.

You Are:

  • Possess a solid technical grounding with hands-on experience of IT Development and/or Operations;
  • A demonstrable track-record and never-ending passion for learning;
  • A self-starter, tech-savvy professional with solid business acumen; ability to articulate Datadog value from server room to boardroom;
  • Confident presentation skills;
  • Must be a current EU resident
  • Desired hands-on experience in two or more of the following areas:
    • Observability: Datadog, Splunk, AppD, New Relic or Dynatrace
    • Public Cloud: AWS, Azure, GCP, or Alibaba
    • Containerization: Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, Cloud Foundry
    • Dev/Scripting: Python, Javascript, Ruby, Perl, PHP, Go
    • Config Mgmt: Terraform, Ansible, Puppet, Chef
    • CI / CD: Jenkins, Gitlab

Bonus Points:

  • Previous experience working in a technical role for or supporting channel partners (Systems Integrators, Managed Services Providers, e.g.);
  • Previous experience using Datadog and/or other cloud monitoring tools (APM, Infrastructure, Logs, Synthetics, NPM);
  • Previous experience with root-cause-analysis, troubleshooting, debugging

Why You Should Apply:

  • Generous and competitive global and US benefits
  • New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan
  • Continuous career development and pathing opportunities
  • Product training to develop an in-depth understanding of our product and space
  • Best in breed onboarding
  • Internal mentor and buddy program cross-departmentally
  • Friendly and inclusive workplace culture

About Datadog:

Datadog is the monitoring and security platform for cloud applications. Our SaaS product is used by organizations of all sizes across a wide range of industries to enable digital transformation, cloud migration, and infrastructure monitoring of our customers’ entire technology stack, allowing for seamless collaboration and problem-solving among Dev, Ops and Security teams globally. Given the resilience of cloud technologies and importance placed today in digital operations and agility, Datadog continues to innovate and is well positioned for the long term.

About Datadog:

Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. Trusted globally by Fortune 500 companies and high-growth AI leaders, Datadog enables businesses to move faster with clarity and confidence. Learn more about #DatadogLife on Instagram, LinkedIn, and Datadog Learning Center.

raw.description:
Vollzeit | Remote möglich | 4.700–5.800 Euro brutto pro Monat

Ein Kunde möchte einen Ablauf automatisieren. Bevor unsere Entwickler loslegen, muss klar sein, wie der Prozess heute funktioniert, was sich verbessern soll und woran wir eine gute Lösung erkennen. Bei Flow Factor übernimmst du diese Klärung gemeinsam mit unseren Kunden.

Du arbeitest direkt mit unseren Kunden und unserem Entwicklungsteam. Wir unterstützen mittelständische Unternehmen im deutschsprachigen Raum bei der Prozessautomatisierung und beim Einsatz von KI. Deine Aufgabe ist es, aus Kundenwünschen konkrete, abgestimmte Anforderungen zu machen und die Umsetzung fachlich zu begleiten.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du führst Gespräche und Workshops mit Kunden, um Ziele, Abläufe und Probleme zu verstehen.

  • Du analysierst bestehende Prozesse, beteiligte Systeme und Datenflüsse und schlägst praktikable Verbesserungen vor.

  • Du formulierst Anforderungen, stimmst die Prioritäten mit dem Kunden und dem Entwicklungsteam ab und hältst Umfang sowie Abnahmekriterien fest.

  • Du besprichst die Anforderungen mit unseren Entwicklern, klärst fachliche Rückfragen und bewertest gemeinsam mit ihnen die Umsetzbarkeit.

  • Du machst Auswirkungen von Änderungswünschen transparent und sorgst dafür, dass Entscheidungen dokumentiert werden.

  • Du begleitest die Umsetzung, prüfst Ergebnisse und führst Kunden durch Demonstrationen und fachliche Abnahmen.

Requirements

Das bringst du mit

  • Du hast bereits Anforderungen in IT- oder Digitalisierungsprojekten aufgenommen und mit einem Umsetzungsteam abgestimmt – etwa als Business Analyst, Requirements Engineer, IT-Berater oder in einer vergleichbaren Rolle.

  • Du kannst Kundengespräche strukturieren und auch unklare oder widersprüchliche Wünsche so klären, dass daraus umsetzbare Aufgaben werden.

  • Du verstehst betriebliche Abläufe und kannst dich in Software, Schnittstellen und Datenflüsse einarbeiten.

  • Du dokumentierst präzise und kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch mit fachlichen Ansprechpartnern und Entwicklern.

  • Du arbeitest eigenständig, sprichst Unklarheiten früh an und hältst Absprachen nach.

Erfahrung mit Prozessautomatisierung oder KI-Anwendungen ist hilfreich. Die technische Architektur entwickelst du gemeinsam mit unserem Entwicklungsteam. Dein Schwerpunkt liegt auf der fachlichen Klärung und der Zusammenarbeit mit dem Kunden.

Das erwartet dich

  • 4.700–5.800 Euro brutto pro Monat in Vollzeit.

  • Die Möglichkeit, remote zu arbeiten; unser Standort ist Grevenbroich.

  • Direkten Austausch mit Kunden und kurze Wege zu den Entwicklern.

  • Eigene Verantwortung für die fachliche Betreuung von Kundenprojekten in einem kleinen Team.

  • Projekte, bei denen du von der ersten Analyse bis zur Abnahme mitwirkst.

Du möchtest Kunden beraten und dafür sorgen, dass Entwickler mit klaren Anforderungen arbeiten können? Dann bewirb dich über das Bewerbungsformular. Besonders interessiert uns, welche Rolle du bisher in Kunden- oder IT-Projekten übernommen hast.

We are looking for a Senior Full-stack engineer (React/Node/.NET) for a client we’ve been collaborating with for 6+ years. Your main responsibility will be collaborating with an already established team of developers from Space Inch’s side reworking the clients systems as they modernize their stack and add new features. The client is in the eCommerce industry, specifically dealing with customized gift cards.

If you're a full-stack engineer with solid knowledge of React / NextJS, Node / NestJS & .NET, and have previously worked on production-level platforms we’d love to talk!

Our Mission, Vision, and Values

At Space Inch, we prioritize alignment with our clients and team, ensuring a deep understanding of their needs. We are committed to delivering exceptional work while supporting the personal and professional growth of our team members. Every team member has access to an executive coach as part of this commitment.

About Working at Space Inch

  • Our team (~60 people) is primarily based in Croatia, with members in South America, Serbia, and the US. While focus is on working remotely, we do have an office in Zagreb for those who prefer a hybrid approach and are located nearby.
  • We work on end-to-end projects with long-term vision
  • We strongly support work/life balance for our team members.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of experience as a full-stack developer
  • Strong experience working with Typescript using React / NextJS
  • Strong experience in Node, specifically using NestJS
  • Strong experience working with .NET, especially rewriting legacy code
  • Experience with MySQL, PostgreSQL
  • Experience with Git and GitHub
  • Proficiency in both spoken and written English
  • Experience working with Fastify
  • Nice to have experience in:
    • Vite
    • Previous work with eCommerce space
  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop robust and scalable full-stack web applications using React / NextJS & Node / NestJS.
  • Work on developing robust and scalable .NET apps and rewriting legacy .NET code
  • Write clean, maintainable, and well-tested code.
  • Contribute to code reviews and provide constructive feedback.

Typical Challenges You'll be Solving

  • Optimizing applications for maximum speed and scalability.
  • Debugging and fixing reported issues in a timely manner.
  • Balancing delivery speed with technical excellence.
  • Ensuring accessibility, responsiveness, and high performance.

Qualities for Success

  • Proactive, solutions-driven mindset.
  • Strong attention to detail and code quality.
  • Comfortable making technical decisions independently.
  • Passion for learning and improving.
  • Ownership mentality — you care about the end product.

Where You've Likely Developed These Skills

  • Digital product agencies or consultancies.
  • Cross-functional product teams building real-world eCommerce platforms.

This Job is Right for You If

  • You thrive in collaborative yet autonomous environments.
  • You enjoy shaping both frontend and backend architecture, keeping in mind best practices for both
  • You value quality and thoughtful delivery over rushing.

This Job is not Right for You If

  • If you prefer solely frontend or backend development.
  • You expect constant supervision or micromanagement.
  • You prefer chaotic startup environments with unclear priorities.

Benefits

What's In It for You

  • Real influence on technical decisions and project direction.
  • Diverse projects with leading US clients.
  • Professional development support (courses, coaching, mentorship).
  • Work-life balance, transparency, and long-term relationships.

Benefits

  • Compensations:$4.500,00 – $6.000/monthly for B2B engagement, based on experience and skills.
  • Remote-first setup
  • Health & Wellbeing: 23 days of PTO + 100% paid sick leave + annual health checkup budget
  • Stay active: Wellness subsidy

raw.description:
Vantor is forging the new frontier of spatial intelligence, helping decision makers and operators navigate what’s happening now and shape what’s coming next. Vantor is a place for problem solvers, changemakers, and go-getters—where people are working together to help our customers see the world differently, and in doing so, be seen differently. Come be part of a mission, not just a job, where you can: Shape your own future, build the next big thing, and change the world.

Please review the job details below.

Vantor is seeking an experienced GEOINT Analyst / Pattern Analysis Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support intelligence, operational planning, and decision-making efforts in GCC. The successful candidate will leverage geospatial intelligence (GEOINT), remote sensing, and pattern analysis methodologies to assess activities, identify trends, and provide actionable intelligence in support of military operations and strategic objectives.

The GEOINT Analyst will analyze satellite imagery, aerial photography, geospatial datasets, and other intelligence sources to identify patterns of life, assess threats, monitor operational environments, and support mission planning. This position requires advanced analytical skills, expertise in geospatial technologies, and the ability to produce high-quality intelligence products for senior military and government stakeholders.

Working Conditions:

  • Position based in GCC.
  • May require periodic travel within the region.
  • Ability to support mission requirements in dynamic operational and military environments.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) analysis in support of military operations, security assessments, and strategic planning activities.
  • Analyze satellite imagery, aerial photography, full-motion video, and other geospatial data sources to identify significant activities, trends, and anomalies.
  • Perform pattern-of-life and pattern analysis to support intelligence collection, targeting, threat assessments, and operational planning.
  • Develop geospatial products, maps, overlays, briefings, and intelligence reports for operational and strategic decision-makers.
  • Integrate geospatial intelligence with multiple intelligence disciplines to provide comprehensive assessments.
  • Conduct predictive geospatial analysis using advanced applications and workflows
  • Evaluate infrastructure, terrain, transportation networks, military installations, and other geographic features relevant to mission requirements.
  • Monitor emerging developments and provide timely assessments of activities impacting regional security and military operations.
  • Support contingency planning, mission analysis, and operational readiness efforts.
  • Present findings and brief intelligence assessments to senior military, government, and organizational leadership.
  • Maintain proficiency with geospatial tools, imagery exploitation techniques, and intelligence methodologies.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Geospatial Intelligence, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Geography, Data Science, Remote Sensing, or a related field.
  • Minimum 8 years of relevant professional experience in geospatial intelligence, imagery analysis, geographic information systems, or related disciplines.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience conducting GEOINT analysis in support of military operations.
  • Demonstrated expertise in imagery interpretation, geospatial analysis, and pattern analysis methodologies.
  • Experience working with geospatial intelligence tools and platforms, including GIS and remote sensing technologies.
  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with experience producing intelligence products and executive-level briefings.
  • Ability to analyze complex datasets and transform findings into actionable intelligence.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting U.S., NATO, Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), or allied military and defense organizations.
  • Advanced experience with ArcGIS, QGIS, ENVI, ERDAS IMAGINE, or similar geospatial analysis platforms.
  • Familiarity with multi-intelligence (multi-INT) fusion and operational intelligence environments.
  • Experience conducting pattern-of-life analysis and activity-based intelligence.
  • Regional expertise related to the Middle East and North Africa (MENA).
  • Professional certifications related to GIS, GEOINT, or geospatial analysis.

EEO Policy: Vantor is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace. We believe in fostering an environment where all team members feel respected, valued, and encouraged to share their ideas. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

About Structured Agency

Structured is a powerhouse of over 50 dedicated professionals with a shared obsession forperformancemarketing. We've carved a niche for ourselves in the ecommerce vertical, marking just the beginning of the many industries we aspire to lead. Our focus centers aroundgrowth—for our clients, our colleagues, and our agency. We are motivated not by obligation to “do our job” but by ambition tobe the bestat our craft. Each of us is on a journey to master our craft, committing the energy, effort, and enthusiasm required to excel.

About the role
At Structured, growth is our primary focus—for our clients and our team. We partner with leading e-commerce brands to build, optimize, and scale their paid media and marketing channels, delivering measurable results that directly move the needle.

If you're a Graphic Designer with an exceptional creative eye, a strategic mindset, and a passion for turning blank canvases into high-converting assets, we want you on our team.

What You'll Do

As a Graphic Designer, you'll collaborate closely with our strategy and copywriting teams to craft stunning, highly functional emails. We're not looking for outdated layouts—we need a designer who understands modern email aesthetics, conversion-focused design, user experience, and what drives engagement right now.

Now, the nitty gritty!

What You'll Bring

  • 3+ years of experience as a Graphic/Visual Designer, ideally in a fast-paced creative agency setting or managing multiple projects and clients
  • Strong foundational design skills with a deep understanding of branding, layout, photography, and high-caliber typography
  • Advanced proficiency in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite
  • Experience designing for e-commerce and performance-driven campaigns
  • Proven ability to quickly context-switch between multiple diverse client accounts without losing momentum or sacrificing quality
  • High attention to detail, with strict standards for design execution, file naming/organization, and presentation
  • Experience with team communication and project management tools (we use Slack and ClickUp!)

Core Responsibilities and Requirements

  • Own your work across accounts fully, taking pride in every piece of creative you deliver
  • Ability to thrive in a remote-first culture—showing up organized, managing your time efficiently, and staying responsive on Slack

Nice to Have

  • Basic motion/GIF animation creation
  • Familiarity with AI tools (like Gemini Pro) for fast storyboarding, generating background assets, or scaling creative variations
  • A sharp eye for flow—spotting when a headline runs too long or a CTA could be punchier to match the visual rhythm

Why Structured

  • Talented Team: Work alongside strategists, designers, and performance experts who love creating high-performing assets and leveling up their craft
  • High-Impact Creative: See the direct results of your work as it drives real revenue for top e-commerce brands
  • Supportive Culture: Clear communication, radical accountability, and a collaborative creative environment define how we work
  • Remote-First: Work from anywhere while staying connected to a high-performing team

This is a fully remote, hourly freelance role. Must be available to work core US hours.

Reports to: VP of Marketing

Location: Remote

Position Overview

The Director of Growth Marketing is an important strategic leader at HealthMark Group not only within the marketing team, but across the organization. This person collaborates cross-functionally as a senior leadership team member to help set strategy and drive the execution of go-to-market objectives.

The central objective of this role is to drive scalable, measurable revenue growth through integrated demand generation, digital marketing and sales-aligned programs. You’ll be responsible for owning the marketing tech stack along with the growth operations function to support the HealthMark growth engine. This is a hands-on leadership role, combining the management of a team with tactical execution, and a successful candidate will be comfortable with that balance. This is very much a player/coach opportunity.

Key Responsibilities

Demand Generation

  • Own, manage and execute a data-driven demand generation strategy designed to increase pipeline contributions YOY
  • Manage current demand generation programs including email, tradeshows, paid digital, website; continuously test and evolve tactics to optimize program success
  • Own a prospecting data strategy, including data enrichment, segmentation, targeting and messaging
  • Support sales enablement through campaigns, content and strategic insights
  • Introduce new demand generation programs
  • Define and implement modern campaigns aligned to target accounts and buying stages

Team and Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Partner with the VP of Marketing to set and manage team objectives and priorities
  • Hire, mentor and manage growth marketing managers and specialists
  • Collaborate with sales leaders to align on go-to-market priorities
  • Partner with leadership on strategic planning, forecasting and resource allocation
  • Play an active role in executive-level growth strategy discussions

Sales & Marketing Operations

  • Own the marketing tech stack including HubSpot and connected tools for data, intent, enrichment and analytics. Provide ongoing oversight for current stack and strategic recommendations for future tool and solution investments.
  • Set a successful AI strategy for your team, leveraging AI to improve speed, quality and insight while building human judgement and oversight into the process
  • Own sales and marketing analytics, reporting and performance tracking; establish reporting cadences to drive accountability and decision-making
  • Design and run A/B tests, conversion rate optimization and attribution modeling

Requirements

  • 10 years of B2B marketing experience, including 4 years leading people and programs
  • Experience in healthcare technology or services, or a similarly highly regulated industry
  • Previous hands- on experience with CRM such as Salesforce or HubSpot
  • Previous experience with Attribution Modeling

Skills

  • Strong analytical mindset with experience in performance tracking and attribution
  • Ability to operate both strategically and tactically in a fast-paced environment
  • Proven success driving pipeline growth in a data-driven marketing environment
  • Attention to detail and organization, both for yourself and for a team
  • Demonstrates a bias for action and quick decision-making under tight deadlines
  • Applies a strong sense of ownership to resolve issues and deliver results swiftly.

Note: This job description is intended to provide a general overview of the position and does not encompass all job-related responsibilities and requirements. The responsibilities and qualifications may be subject to change as the needs of the organization evolve.

The incumbent must demonstrate a strong understanding of confidentiality requirements, adhere to all HIPAA regulations and organizational privacy and security policies, and report any known or suspected unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of PHI immediately to the Privacy Officer or Information Security team. raw.title: Senior Evaluation Manager for Sponsored Research
raw.excerpt: For over 35 years, Youth Villages has transformed the lives of children and families nationwide through innovative, research-based programs focused on preserving and restoring families.
raw.description:
For over 35 years, Youth Villages has transformed the lives of children and families nationwide through innovative, research-based programs focused on preserving and restoring families.

As a national leader in children’s mental and behavioral health, we serve more than 47,000 youth, young people, and their families annually across 29 states and Washington, D.C. Our proven treatment models drive long-term success in child welfare, juvenile justice, and mental health systems. At Youth Villages, we do what works — partnering with others to expand our impact and advocate for meaningful, lasting change.

We're seeking purpose-driven individuals who are passionate about making a difference. With a dedicated team of more than 5,000 staff, Youth Villages is committed to investing in and supporting our employees by offering opportunities to build a fulfilling career through professional growth, personal development, and a mission that matters— helping children and families live successfully.

For more information, please visit

Position Overview:

Youth Villages is seeking a strategic, highly organized Senior Evaluation Manager for Sponsored Research to lead complex evaluation initiatives that support program improvement, service expansion, and child welfare system change. Reporting to the Director of Research, the person in this role will provide scientific and project leadership for evaluations conducted in partnership with external researchers, ensuring that studies address meaningful organizational questions, use rigorous and appropriate methods, and produce findings that can inform implementation, scaling, practice, and policy.

The Senior Evaluation Manager for Sponsored Research will serve as Youth Villages’ primary liaison with external evaluation partners as part of one or more externally funded projects and will integrate evidence across evaluations, administrative data analyses, implementation findings, and other sources. A key responsibility will be synthesizing this evidence into comprehensive products that explain what is changing, how strategies are being implemented, whether expected results are occurring, and what can be learned to strengthen future efforts.

This is a remote position, with occasional travel required for meetings, presentations, conferences, and other dissemination activities.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:


I. Provide Strategic and Scientific Leadership for Evaluation

  • Develop and manage evaluation learning agendas that identify priority questions, evidence needs, measurement strategies, and major milestones.
  • Ensure evaluations address specific strategic, programmatic, implementation, practice, or policy questions.
  • Provide scientific guidance on evaluation design, measurement, quantitative and qualitative methods, analytic approaches, and interpretation.
  • Critically evaluate methodological approaches, assumptions, findings, and limitations and facilitate resolution of methodological questions with research partners.
  • Ensure evaluation partners have the programmatic, operational, organizational, and system context needed to design studies and appropriately interpret findings.
  • Identify emerging evaluation needs and work with partners to refine research questions, measures, and analytic approaches as findings and priorities evolve.

II. Lead Sponsored Evaluation Partnerships and Projects

  • Serve as Youth Villages’ primary liaison with the external evaluator for the Intercept Scaling and Practice/Policy Change investment.
  • Coordinate evaluation activities across Youth Villages teams, external evaluators, research partners, and other collaborators.
  • Manage project plans, timelines, deliverables, dependencies, responsibilities, decisions, and communications across multiple evaluation workstreams.
  • Ensure partners receive timely feedback, decisions, contextual information, data coordination, and access to appropriate Youth Villages staff and stakeholders.
  • Maintain clear documentation of research questions, methodological decisions, findings, open questions, and next steps.
  • Proactively identify competing priorities, barriers, and delays and assess implications for commitments, staffing, budgets, and timelines.
  • Lead regular partnership check-ins and contribute to assessment of partnership effectiveness and progress toward shared goals.

III. Integrate Evidence Across Sources

  • Integrate findings across evaluation studies, administrative data analyses, implementation measures, qualitative research, and other evidence sources to develop a comprehensive understanding of progress and outcomes.
  • Coordinate with colleagues leading complementary research and evidence-building initiatives to align questions, measures, timelines, and interpretation where work intersects.
  • Examine evidence across multiple levels, including implementation, program outcomes, organizational and system change, and broader child welfare outcomes.
  • Help distinguish whether unexpected findings may reflect the strategy itself, implementation, underlying assumptions, measurement, or contextual factors.
  • Identify areas of convergence, inconsistency, and remaining uncertainty across evidence sources and work with research partners to determine appropriate next questions.
  • Lead development of integrated evaluation products that synthesize findings across research partners and data sources.

IV. Translate Evidence into Organizational Learning and Action

  • Help teams use evaluation findings to assess whether strategies should be continued, strengthened, adapted, or reconsidered.
  • Translate findings into clear implications for implementation, scaling, program improvement, practice, policy, and future research.
  • Develop presentations, executive summaries, reports, and other evidence products for leadership, practitioners, funders, public-system partners, and other non-technical audiences.
  • Coordinate interpretation and dissemination of findings across research partners and Youth Villages teams, collaborating with Communications and other teams as appropriate.
  • Identify opportunities to synthesize lessons across projects and contribute to broader organizational learning about effective implementation and scaling.

Qualifications:

  • Doctorate in psychology, public policy, public administration, social work, epidemiology, or a related social or behavioral science field is required, with 5+ years of relevant experience.
  • Strong knowledge of research design, quantitative methods, program evaluation, and qualitative or mixed-methods research is required.
  • Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate research methods, measurement strategies, analytic approaches, and the strength and limitations of evidence is required.
  • Knowledge of implementation science and/or applied research methods; experience evaluating complex interventions, implementation efforts, or systems-change initiatives preferred.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with demonstrated ability to coordinate multiple research workstreams, partners, timelines, and priorities is required.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with researchers, organizational leaders, practitioners, and other stakeholders is required.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical information for non-technical audiences is essential.
  • Experience working with child welfare systems or other public human-services systems strongly preferred.

Work Environment

Work must be performed from a secure, private home office workplace with a reliable high-speed internet connection. Environment should have moderate noise level consistent with a standard home office


Physical Demands

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary seated position for an extended period
  • Frequent and continuous use of hands, wrists, and fingers to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other standard office equipment
  • Continuous near vision required for reading computer screens and documents. Constant ability to hear and speak clearly during meetings (including virtual meetings) and phone calls
  • Occasional moving about workspace
  • Occasional lifting or carrying of light office supplies, files, or laptop equipment, typically weighing less than 15 pounds

Youth Villages Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Prescription Drug Coverage and Vision

  • 401(k)

  • Time off:

    • 2 week paid vacation (full-time) / 1 week paid vacation (part-time)

    • 12 paid sick days per year

    • 11 paid holidays

  • Paid Parental Leave

  • Mileage & Cell Phone Reimbursement (when applicable)

  • Tuition reimbursement and licensure supervision

  • Growth & development through continuous training

  • Clinical and administrative advancement opportunities

*Benefits are excluded for variable status employees.

Youth Villages is an equal opportunity employer and provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Youth Villages is committed to not only advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace but also in our work with children and young adults. We know that children, families and young people of color can face inequity in child welfare and justice systems, and we train our employees to build the skills they need to work with the communities that we serve, as well as, other employees from different cultures and backgrounds. Youth Villages is opposed to racism in any of its forms and is committed to inclusion, equity, and diversity. We believe that respect for each other is crucial in the work that we do each day.

raw.title: Graduate Engineer
raw.excerpt: We’re looking for high-potential final-year students and recent graduates with strong problem-solving skills who can grow into outstanding technical contributors at CloudLinux.
raw.description:
We’re looking for high-potential final-year students and recent graduates with strong problem-solving skills who can grow into outstanding technical contributors at CloudLinux. This is a paid, full-time graduate role and a first step into professional engineering. You’ll work on real products, learn alongside experienced engineers and deepen your technical skills in areas such as Linux, open-source software and security.

We’re looking for people who combine strong independent thinking with the ability to use AI confidently to tackle complex technical problems — understanding unfamiliar code, developing solutions and critically evaluating the results.

Who we are

CloudLinux is a global remote-first company. We are driven by our principles: do the right thing, employees first, we are remote first, and we deliver high-volume, low-cost Linux infrastructure and security products that help companies to increase the efficiency of their operations. Every person on our team supports each other and does what we can to ensure we all are successful.

Check out our website for more information.

What you'll do

You’ll join an engineering team working on Linux infrastructure and security for web hosting. Our products include CloudLinux OS, which helps hosting providers manage server resources and isolate hosting accounts, and Imunify, which protects servers and websites against malware and attacks.

You don’t need prior experience in these specific areas. We’re looking for strong engineering potential — how you approach unfamiliar problems, learn quickly and use AI thoughtfully. We’ll consider your challenge results, interests and strengths alongside the opportunities available across our engineering teams.

Experienced engineers on your team will help you get to know our codebase, tools and the way we work.

Depending on the team you join, your work may include:

  • Developing and testing product features, fixes and engineering tools.
  • Investigating production issues, tracing their causes and implementing reliable solutions.
  • Reading unfamiliar code and understanding how different parts of a system interact.
  • Improving automation for building, testing and delivering software.
  • Contributing to code reviews and technical discussions.

Requirements

What we’re looking for:

  • Practical programming skills in at least one language, such as C, C++, Python or Go, whether from coursework, personal projects or early hands-on experience.
  • Strong analytical thinking, solid fundamentals in algorithms and data structures, and a structured approach to solving problems.
  • The ability to use AI tools to work through unfamiliar programming problems, critically assess and improve their output, and explain and test the resulting solution.
  • Curiosity, the ability to learn independently, and persistence when a solution isn’t immediately clear.
  • Care for code quality and the ability to carry a task through to a working, tested solution.
  • Clear communication and the ability to explain technical decisions.
  • English at B2 level or higher.

We’re looking for people at the very start of their engineering careers. We’re open to:

  • Final-year students.
  • Recent graduates.

This is a full-time position, including for candidates who are still completing their studies.

What may help you stand out

Any of the following can strengthen your application, although none is mandatory:

  • A degree (or final-year standing) in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent skills you can demonstrate through your projects and code.
  • Personal or academic software projects, especially ones whose design decisions you can explain.
  • Contributions to open-source projects, even small ones.
  • Participation in CTF competitions, hackathons, or a homelab you administer.
  • Evidence that you’ve taught yourself a language, stack or system in depth because a problem demanded it.
  • A strong interest in Linux, operating systems, networking or security — including relevant coursework, a thesis, research or personal projects.

If your CV doesn’t fully capture your potential, apply anyway. Show us what you’ve built, the hard problems you’ve solved, and what makes you different from other engineers at a similar stage of their career.

How selection works

What you build counts for more than your CV.

  • Apply in a couple of minutes — autofill from your CV or LinkedIn.
  • We take a quick first look at each application. Candidates who look like a fit get a personal link to our engineering challenge, which carries the most weight in our assessment. You can start whenever you’re ready within the access window.
  • You’ll have up to 3 hours for the challenge. It is modelled on a real problem from our security products — one our engineers have already solved in production. Your work won’t be used in our products; it is used only to assess your approach and skills.
  • The task unfolds in phases, with changing requirements. It is deliberately larger than anyone can finish — we look at what you prioritise and why, not at whether you complete every part.
  • AI tools are expected, not just allowed. We’re interested in your judgment: what you accept, reject and verify, and how you defend your trade-offs.
  • Candidates whose challenge results demonstrate a strong match are invited to interview with our senior engineers and HR.

The challenge is designed to give you an opportunity to demonstrate your practical skills, judgment and potential.

Benefits

What's in it for you?

  • Fully remote work with flexible hours — schedule your day and work from anywhere in the world.
  • 24 paid vacation days a year, 10 national holidays, and unlimited sick leave.
  • Compensation for private medical insurance.
  • Co-working and gym/sports reimbursement.
  • A dedicated education budget.
  • A reward for the most innovative idea the company can patent.
  • A real focus on professional development, on interesting and challenging projects.

By applying for this position, you consent to the processing of your personal data as described in our Privacy Policy (, which provides detailed information on how we maintain and handle your data.

What’s the role

Shell is seeking a Director, Regulatory Carbon (also known internally as Regulatory Manager, Carbon) to join its team in Houston, Texas, or San Diego, California.

This role supports the SEAm Environmental Products Trading, RNG Origination, and Renewable & Energy Solutions businesses by monitoring market activities and regulatory changes, advocating externally for competitive markets, communicating regulatory updates and their impacts to commercial teams, advising on regulatory matters to facilitate commercial transactions within existing regulations across the Americas, and overseeing compliance obligations and reporting requirements.


This role is preferably based in Houston, Texas or San Diego, California, but can also be performed remotely.


Accountabilities:

  • Serve as the primary regulatory advisor to the Commercial team to understand Shell’s commercial position and the key regulatory drivers that impact portfolio performance and risk. Be proactive in advising Commercial team of potential changes in regulatory landscape and coordinating with team to develop appropriate responses
  • Monitor and analyze legislative, regulatory, and political developments affecting cap-and-trade carbon markets, clean fuel programs, RNG, and communicate business impacts to internal stakeholders. (Focus: 80% Carbon and 20% RNG/clean fuels)
  • Provide regulatory guidance and market intelligence to the environmental products trading team, RNG origination, and power trading teams to support commercial decision-making and risk management
  • Track and evaluate proposed and developing policy, legislative and market developments across major North American carbon programs (California cap-and-Invest, WA cap-and-Invest, RGGI, Quebec cap and trade) and provide timely analysis to support the carbon trading desk’s positioning
  • Evaluate proposed and developing regulatory programs across North America to determine potential impacts on carbon allowances and offsets, renewable natural gas, low-carbon fuel credits, environmental attributes, and related trading activities
  • Develop and advocate policy positions through participation in regulatory proceedings, legislative processes, trade associations, and stakeholder engagements, in coordination with Corporate Relations and Government Relations teams
  • Build and maintain relationships with regulators, policymakers, market administrators, industry stakeholders, and trade associations to advance Shell Energy's commercial and policy objectives. Serve on trade association and 501(c)(3) boards of directors, deriving benefits from memberships while coordinating advocacy efforts and building consensus within these groups
  • Monitor regulatory reporting obligations and support the preparation, verification, and submission of required greenhouse gas reports
  • Assess and coordinate implementation of new regulatory requirements, ensuring affected business teams understand compliance obligations and operational impacts
  • Oversee carbon allowance and credit transfer activities in the United States and Canada, including associated reporting and recordkeeping requirements
  • Prepare and submit agency reports, permits, and licenses as needed
  • Coordinate development of and work with others to provide regulatory training
  • Review rules affecting implementation of projects being evaluated

What you bring

  • Must have legal authorization to work in the US on a full-time basis for anyone other than current employer
  • Bachelor’s degree or higher required (Business or Law/Policy or equivalent preferred)
  • Minimum of 10 years industry experience in carbon markets
  • In-depth technical and commercial understanding of carbon markets - California cap-and-Invest, WA cap-and-Invest, RGGI, and/or Quebec cap and trade
  • Good technical and commercial understanding of clean fuel programs, RNG markets, and greenhouse gas accounting frameworks. Deep knowledge of existing and emerging regulations in U.S. and Canada. Familiarity of regulatory programs in Europe and Asia, including the ability to assess commercial implications of proposed policy changes is a plus
  • Familiarity with greenhouse gas accounting methodologies, lifecycle carbon intensity frameworks, emissions reporting protocols, sustainability certification programs, and environmental claims requirements to support market participation and compliance is a plus
  • Proven ability to translate complex regulatory developments into actionable commercial recommendations and identify opportunities that create competitive advantage
  • Strong strategic thinking skills, including the ability to anticipate regulatory shifts and assess potential commercial impacts
  • Appreciation of license to operate concerns and compliance
  • Ability to build and foster relationships across various internal and external stakeholders. Strong personal relationships and ability to effectively coordinate with colleagues
  • Ability to effectively operate within a challenging and dynamic work environment including managing competing priorities over a wide spectrum of issues and supporting group efforts on others
  • Fundamental understanding of regulatory processes and procedures and strong research, writing and communication skills

What we offer

The base salary range for this position is $149,000 - $223,000 per year. Individual pay will be based on various factors, such as relevant work experience, education, certifications, skill level, seniority, and internal equity.

For regular full-time or regular part-time employees of the Company (participating companies as listed in the Summary Plan Description), insurance coverage options include medical, dental, vision coverage, life Insurance, Business Travel Accident Insurance, and Occupational Accidental Death Benefit programs. Employees also participate in a company pension plan and a 401(k) plan. Paid leave includes up to 6 weeks of paid vacation time, up to 11 paid holidays, and parental leave offering 16 weeks of paid leave for birthing parents, and 8 weeks of paid leave for non-birthing parents.

Additionally, employees are eligible for short-term disability leave for up to 26 weeks at 100% or 50% of base pay as well as Long-Term Disability insurance. Shell also offers other compensation such financial reimbursement for adoption, wellness, education, and personal learning expenses, and some roles are eligible for discretionary long-term incentives. For interns, eligible benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, life insurance, Business Travel Accident Insurance, and Occupational Accidental Death Benefit programs; participation in a 401(k) plan; and paid leave for up to 11 paid holidays. Additional information on Shell’s US benefit programs can be found at

You bring your skills and experience to Shell and in return you work with talented, committed people on one of the most important challenges facing our planet. You’ll have the opportunity to develop the skills you need to grow in an environment where we value honesty, integrity, and respect for one another. You’ll be able to balance your priorities as you become the best version of yourself.

  • Progress as a person as we work on the energy transition together

  • Achieve your balance in a values-led culture that encourages you to be the best version of yourself

Shell in The United States

With more than 11,000 employees, Shell has been in the US for more than 100 years and is delivering secure energy supplies across America.

From producing a reliable supply of oil and gas in the US Gulf of America to biofuels, our retail sites and EV charging network, to marketing and trading electricity generated by gas plants, solar and wind power, we are one of the few countries where every Shell business is represented.

We are working with our customers to deliver the energy the world needs today and building the energy systems of tomorrow, all while creating value for society and shareholders.

Job Description

Are you curious, motivated, and forward-thinking? At FIS you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and relevant issues in financial services and technology. Our talented people empower us, and we believe in being part of a team that is open, collaborative, entrepreneurial, passionate and above all fun.

About the Team

The Pricing Strategy team is responsible for defining and evolving product- and solution-level pricing frameworks across FIS’s portfolio, with a focus on Banking, Payments, and Wealth solutions. The team works upstream of deal execution and partners closely with product, commercial, and finance leaders to ensure pricing is scalable, consistent, and aligned to customer value. This role will help shape how FIS prices, packages, and monetizes banking products and services across new and existing client segments.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Develop and execute pricing strategies for banking products and services across new and existing client segments, working within broader portfolio and business objectives.
  • Maintain and update list prices, rate cards, pricing metrics, and supporting documentation across the banking product portfolio.
  • Build and refine scalable pricing models using subscription, transaction-based, tiered, usage-based, and enterprise pricing structures.
  • Support packaging and monetization initiatives by evaluating product bundles, feature differentiation, pricing metrics, and customer segment needs.
  • Conduct value-based pricing assessments, competitive benchmarking, customer and market research, and financial analysis to inform pricing recommendations.
  • Partner with product teams to incorporate product capabilities, customer value propositions, and go-to-market plans into pricing analyses and proposals.
  • Review pricing structures across product lines to identify opportunities for standardization, simplification, and improved consistency.
  • Analyze pricing performance, customer adoption, revenue, and profitability to identify opportunities for ongoing optimization.
  • Prepare business cases, pricing proposals, and presentations that clearly communicate analytical findings and recommendations.
  • Work with finance, commercial, sales, and operational teams to support the implementation and ongoing management of approved pricing changes.

What You Bring

  • 3–5+ years of experience in pricing strategy, product strategy, commercial strategy, or financial analysis.
  • Experience in banking, financial technology, payments, or adjacent financial services industries strongly preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of pricing strategy concepts, including value-based pricing, customer segmentation, competitive positioning, and price architecture.
  • Demonstrated experience designing or managing subscription, transaction-based, tiered, usage-based, or enterprise pricing models.
  • Advanced analytical and financial modeling skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear strategic insights and recommendations.
  • Ability to understand product capabilities and customer value drivers and convert them into differentiated packaging and monetization approaches.
  • Experience working in a cross-functional, product-driven environment and influencing stakeholders across product, finance, sales, and commercial teams.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing clear, executive-ready presentations.
  • Bachelor’s degree in finance, economics, business, or another quantitative field, or equivalent practical experience.

Added Bonus If You Have

  • Direct experience with core banking platforms, digital banking solutions, transaction processing, or other banking technology products.
  • Experience supporting a major product launch, portfolio transformation, or migration to a new commercial model.
  • Familiarity with pricing governance processes, configure-price-quote tools, billing systems, or enterprise rate-card administration.
  • Experience with SQL, R, Python, or data-visualization tools is a plus.

What We Offer You

At FIS, you can learn, grow, and make an impact in your career. Our benefits include:

  • Flexible and creative work environment.
  • Diverse and collaborative atmosphere.
  • Professional and personal development resources.
  • Opportunities to volunteer and support charities.
  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.
  • Opportunities to influence pricing strategy and monetization decisions across a global financial technology leader.
  • Exposure to senior leaders and strategic initiatives shaping the future of FIS banking solutions.
FIS is committed to providing its employees with an exciting career opportunity and competitive compensation. The pay range for this full-time position is $151,020.00 - $256,740.00 and reflects the minimum and maximum target for new hire salaries for this position based on the posted role, level, and location. Within the range, actual individual starting pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Any changes in work location will also impact actual individual starting pay. Please consult with your recruiter about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

Privacy Statement

FIS is committed to protecting the privacy and security of all personal information that we process in order to provide services to our clients. For specific information on how FIS protects personal information online, please see the Online Privacy Notice.

EEOC Statement

FIS is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, genetic information, national origin, disability, veteran status, and other protected characteristics. Sourcing Model

Recruitment at FIS works primarily on a direct sourcing model; a relatively small portion of our hiring is through recruitment agencies. raw.description:
About us

Living in a Bubble designs premium campervan and outdoor accessories: magnetic window covers, flyscreens and storage made to fit specific vans. We sell online in Australia and the US to a community of travellers who live, work and holiday in their vans. We are a small remote team, and our founders are hands-on every day.

The role

You are the voice of Living in a Bubble on the phone, and the person customers trust to tell them what fits their van.

The role is phonI'm now starting the hiring for the senior Customer Service and Phone Specialist. Here's the job description. Help me fill out the Asana tasks associated with it.e first, but around half of your day is written: email, chat and social messages. You work alongside our Customer Service Specialist and report directly to our co-founder. There is no team to manage. This is a hands-on role for someone who loves talking to customers and getting the details right.

Our customers: many are retired Australians and Americans, often from regional areas, with STRONG accents. They call because they want to speak to a real person before spending $500 to $1,500 on their van. They value warmth, patience and getting it right the first time.

What you will do

Phone and pre-sales

  • Return calls and voicemails quickly (within 5 minutes during business hours).
  • Answer "will it fit my van?" using our fitment guide: ask the right questions, check, then answer with confidence.
  • Help customers choose the right products and bundles, take orders over the phone and follow up quotes.
  • Explain how our products work and how to install them, before and after purchase.

Written support

  • Reply to emails, chat and social messages in a warm, plain and personal tone.
  • Handle order updates, returns, replacements and delivery issues within our policies and approval limits.

Keeping things right, and making them better

  • Keep our SOPs, reply templates and fitment guide up to date as products and rules change.
  • Spot recurring problems (fit issues, delivery delays, product faults), raise them with evidence, and push for the fix.
  • Track response time, customer satisfaction and phone orders, and send a short weekly update to our co-founder.
  • Review a sample of team replies each week and share feedback.
  • Share what customers are telling us with our product and operations teams.

Requirements

What you need

Essential

  • Excellent spoken English, easily understood by Australian and US customers, and comfortable with strong Australian accents. This is non-negotiable. Expect a live phone assessment.
  • Excellent written English. You will write as much as you speak.
  • At least 3 years in a phone-based customer service or sales role as your main job, not occasional calls alongside email.
  • A track record of phone sales or retention against a target.
  • High attention to detail.
  • You learn technical products quickly

Strongly preferred

  • Experience on Australian-facing accounts (BPO, telco, banking, airlines or retail).
  • Experience with e-commerce or considered purchases, where customers ask a lot of questions before they buy.
  • Have interest in vehicles, makes, etc.

Nice to have (we will train you)

  • Gorgias or a similar helpdesk, Shopify, Asana and Slack.

How we work

  • Remote, based in the Philippines. Full time, 40 hours a week.
  • Monday to Friday, 8:00am to 5:00pm Brisbane time (6:00am to 3:00pm Philippine time), with a one hour break.
  • During work hours you reply on Slack within 10 minutes.
  • A structured 4 week onboarding with product samples sent to you and a written training plan.
  • Start date: early January 2027.

Benefits

What we offer

  • A full-time remote role with a stable, long-term team.
  • A clear path to Customer Service Lead, with a pay review when you step up.
  • Day shift, Monday to Friday. No nights shifts
  • A direct line to our co-founder and real ownership of the customer phone experience.
  • Paid training and onboarding, with product samples sent to you
  • After your 6 month probation: 13th month pay; HMO; paid leave; vacation leave; seasonal performance bonuses.

Our hiring process

  1. Screening questions
  2. One-person interview questions
  3. 20-minute live phone role play with a strong Australian accent where you will need to help customer and sell the products
  4. Final interview with our co-founder
  5. References checked by phone.

raw.description:
Overview

Senior Production Support Analyst

(Remote)

About Us:

Matrix Medical Network is the nation’s leading independent provider of comprehensive in-home health assessments, serving Medicare Advantage, Managed Medicaid and Commercial patients across all 50 states. With a network of 3,000 + clinicians, we deliver personalized Whole Person Care that includes diagnostic testing, risk identification, medication management and preventive health education, empowering people to better manage acute and chronic conditions. Guided by our mantra- We see you. We hear you. We’ve got you.- and our core values of Integrity, Accountability, Trust, Respect and Passion, we are committed to creating a culture where both patients and teammates feel valued, supported and heard.

Why Work at Matrix?

  • The opportunity to work with one of the fastest growing companies in healthcare whose vision is to provide unparalleled quality and value to providers and members.
  • A chance to work with great people on exciting projects.
  • Our opportunities allow you to leverage your expertise and compassion, making a direct impact to the health and well-being of members.
  • Competitive Compensation: Be rewarded for your effort and passion while making a difference in the community.

Responsibilities

About the role:

Type: Full Time, Salary

Compensation: $101,000-$151,000; Bonus 10%

Location: Fully Remote, must be in the United States

Hours: Full Time Days

Benefits Offered to include: Medical, Dental, Vision, paid time off, paid holidays, 401K with company matching, voluntary life insurance, short term disability, long term disability, employee assistance program, health savings account, flexible spending accounts, additional voluntary benefits available.

What to expect:

The Senior Production Support Analyst is the senior operational owner for the member scheduling and access platform, the front door of the member journey, covering scheduling for in-home and telehealth assessments, primary care visits, and quality and care-gap closure visits. The analyst leads Tier 2 and Tier 3 incident response, owns root cause and problem management, and sets the monitoring, runbook, and release validation standards for the platform and its integrations.

The role works daily with the Senior Product Owner, the scheduling platform engineering team, the central Data and Quality Assurance (QA) teams, the IT Service Desk, and external scheduling and health plan partners. Because scheduling failures reduce completed visits, the analyst ties incident and defect data to conversion impact so the Senior Product Owner can prioritize fixes on measurable outcomes. The analyst also mentors less experienced support staff.

Systems and Processes Supported

  • Core scheduling platform: initial scheduling, in-home and telehealth assessment scheduling, and quality and care-gap closure visit scheduling.
  • Provider access and demand-capture scheduling engine: geographic capacity balancing, progressive scheduling windows, and travel versus non-travel service rules.
  • Real-time scheduling integrations with health plan partners, and the partner API gateway.
  • Self-service channels: SMS self-scheduling, the member self-scheduling portal, and the preference center.
  • External integrations with EHR platforms and third-party consumer scheduling networks.
  • The platform’s event-driven architecture, and the canonical data standards and test automation practices shared with the central Data and QA teams.
  • Agile delivery with the engineering team: sprints, backlog grooming, and release planning.

Responsibilities

  • Lead Tier 2 and Tier 3 incident intake, triage, and diagnosis. Act as incident lead on high-severity events, coordinating engineering, partners, and business stakeholders through resolution and post-incident review.
  • Monitor platform availability, SMS delivery, the member portal, provider capacity outputs, event processing, and health plan, EHR, and scheduling network integration feeds. Define alert thresholds, service level indicators, and dashboards with engineering.
  • Diagnose integration failures by analyzing API requests, responses, logs, and event flows to determine whether a fault sits in the platform, a partner system, or the data.
  • Resolve complex scheduling data errors, including duplicate or orphaned appointments, capacity and scheduling window rule errors, and member access cases, using SQL and approved tooling under PHI handling controls. Build repeatable fixes in place of one-off corrections.
  • Own problem management. Lead root cause analysis with engineering, track repeat incidents to closure, and submit findings to the Senior Product Owner as prioritized backlog items with defined impact.
  • Quantify conversion impact. Use scheduling and outreach analytics to measure how incidents and defects affect scheduling conversion and completed visits, and supply that data to the Senior Product Owner’s conversion optimization work and business cases.
  • Serve as first contact and escalation point for health plan, EHR, and scheduling network partners. Track partner SLAs and open items to closure and lead partner troubleshooting.
  • Take part in sprint ceremonies, backlog grooming, and release planning. Define production readiness and validation criteria, validate releases, run smoke tests with QA, and watch for post-release regressions. Recommend test automation coverage with the central Data and QA teams.
  • Own runbooks, known-issue lists, and escalation paths. Automate recurring support tasks with scripting and AI-enabled productivity tools where appropriate.
  • Report monthly to the Senior Product Owner and IT leadership on incidents, root causes, repeat issues, mean time to detect and resolve, and engineering time spent on production issues.
  • Mentor and train support staff and the IT Service Desk on platform triage, and document knowledge so coverage does not depend on one person.
  • Work with the IT Service Desk on assigned items and meet all Service Level Agreements.
  • Follow corporate security policies and HIPAA requirements when handling protected health information (PHI).
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of technical support experience in a corporate environment, including at least 3 years in Tier 2, Tier 3, or production support for business-critical applications.
  • 3+ years writing SQL queries, including joins and common table expressions, to diagnose and resolve data issues in production.
  • Demonstrated experience leading high-severity incidents and conducting root cause analysis and post-incident reviews.
  • Proven ability to identify trends in submitted issues, document them clearly, and present findings to Product Management and Product Engineering teams in a format that supports prioritization decisions.
  • Experience with an IT service management or ticketing tool and with incident, problem, and change management practices aligned to ITIL.
  • Hands-on experience troubleshooting API and system integrations, including request, response, and log analysis, and working with external partners to resolve failures.
  • Experience with monitoring and alerting tools and log analysis.
  • Experience working with engineering teams in an Agile or Scrum model, using Jira or Azure DevOps.
  • Experience supporting systems that handle PHI, with working knowledge of HIPAA requirements.
  • Ability to communicate incident status and business impact to senior leadership, and to write clear runbooks and root cause reports.
  • Strong troubleshooting, decision-making, and independent judgment, with the ability to prioritize in a fast-paced, changing environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting healthcare scheduling, contact center, or EHR integration technology.
  • Experience supporting event-driven or message-based architectures, including queues and event streams.
  • Experience with conversion funnel or outreach analytics, and reporting tools such as SQL Reporting Services.
  • Scripting experience (Python or PowerShell) to automate support tasks.
  • Experience with generative AI and AI-enabled productivity platforms.
  • Experience with Internet Information Services (IIS), and reading or debugging Java or VB/.NET code.
  • Experience mentoring or leading less experienced support staff.

Certifications (Preferred)

  • ITIL 4 Foundation or higher.
  • AI or automation-related certification.

Education

Bachelor’s degree preferred (Information Technology, Computer Science, Health Informatics, or a related field), or equivalent experience in a senior application or production support role with SQL troubleshooting, ideally in healthcare.

Our Culture:

  • We have a clear vision of where we are going, and we are guided by core values that embody our organization and our culture.
  • We emphasizes innovation and growth, and you will be given the opportunities and tools to develop personally and professionally.
  • We encourage and celebrate collaboration.
  • We have a deep commitment to positively impact the communities in which we work and to make a difference in the lives of who we serve.

It is the policy of Matrix to provide equal employment opportunities without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, genetic information or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. About the Role

This is a high-impact role that helps define how CoLab delivers technical value to its most strategic customers. You'll act as a dedicated technical problem-solver and trusted advisor, embedding with enterprise customers to optimize how they use CoLab—especially our AI tools.

You'll help large mechanical engineering orgs rethink how they manage feedback, data, and decision-making across design and PLM. That means getting deep into customer workflows, testing new ways of working, and building repeatable methods the rest of the team can scale.

You'll work within our forward deployed team, alongside a technical program manager, software FDE, and customer-facing teams to close technical gaps, shape product direction, and directly influence customer success. This role isn't about selling or pitching—it's about deeply understanding engineering problems and solving them alongside the customer.

Our Ideal Candidate

You're a mechanical engineer by trade but your superpower is applying that knowledge in creative, systems-level ways. You're curious, technical, and comfortable working through ambiguity. You've likely been a design engineer or worked in a PLM-heavy environment. Maybe you've dabbled in automation, scripting, or app development for internal tools.

You don't need to be the loudest voice in the room—but you can run a sprint, lead a cross-functional project, and talk shop with both customer engineers and internal developers.

If the average person might find this job too undefined or complex, that probably excites you.

Job Responsibilities

  • Embed with enterprise customers to optimize CoLab usage, with a focus on AI tools like AutoReview and Operator.
  • Investigate and solve complex engineering data and integration challenges across PLM, ERP, QMS, and traditional design feedback tools.
  • Partner with a cross functional team to test and implement new CoLab workflows inside customer environments
  • Collaborate with product teams to identify feature gaps, improve capabilities, and refine AutoReview
  • Build technical documentation, playbooks, and repeatable frameworks based on successful projects
  • Provide mechanical engineering expertise to validate AI-generated results and ensure engineering rigor

Qualifications

Must-haves:

  • Background in mechanical design engineering, ideally in a medium to large sized organization.
  • Strong understanding of PLM systems and enterprise engineering data architecture
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and cross-functional collaborations
  • Experience working directly with customers or internal stakeholders to solve technical problems
  • Comfort working in fast-changing, ambiguous environments
  • Strong written communication and documentation skills
  • Working knowledge of high level AI architecture, specifically LLMs.
  • Familiarity with APIs, data integrations, and enterprise architecture concepts

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with internal tool development, scripting, or automation
  • Exposure to AI/ML tools applied to engineering workflows
  • Prior work in design consulting or product development at scale

Extra Details

  • This is a full-time, permanent position with a competitive compensation package that includes stock options
  • Unlimited paid vacation, extended health benefits, and RRSP/401k matching
  • Remote-friendly within Eastern or Central time zones in Canada or the US.
  • This role will have a travel component to visit customers onsite. Customer visits are typically 1-3 days total, one or two a month.

Equity Note

Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic and apply even if you don't meet every single qualification—your potential is what matters most to us.

raw.description:
About Givebacks, Inc.

Givebacks is a mission-driven software company rethinking how K–12 school communities manage payments and fundraising. We build simple, transparent tools that bring districts, parent organizations, and families together in one unified platform—cutting through complexity so schools can spend less time on admin work and more time supporting students. We’re a growing, ambitious team focused on building thoughtfully, moving quickly, and creating meaningful impact in school communities.

We are seeking a driven and research-oriented Market Development Associate to support district-level revenue growth through targeted, state-specific go-to-market execution. This role is a critical pipeline-generating partner to Sales and Marketing, responsible for building research-backed outreach strategies, executing outbound campaigns, and supporting conference-driven demand generation.

The ideal candidate is a high-urgency, self-directed operator who thrives on research, execution, and continuous improvement. This role is well-suited for someone early in their sales or go-to-market career who wants clear expectations, measurable impact, and exposure to strategic sales motions in a fast-growing EdTech company.

What You’ll Do:

Market & State-Level Strategy

  • Conduct deep research into state-specific K–12 policies, procedures, and operational nuances related to fundraisers, boosters, and school districts.
  • Build, document, and maintain comprehensive state-by-state sales strategies within HubSpot.
  • Prioritize and sequence state outreach based on opportunity size, readiness, and ease of entry.
  • Partner with Marketing to align messaging and campaigns with state-level insights.

Pipeline Generation & Prospecting

  • Research district and school-level decision-makers and accurately import contact data into HubSpot.
  • Add a minimum of 1,700 new school buildings into the pipeline by driving qualified discovery meetings.
  • Execute outbound email and call sequences with consistency, urgency, and attention to detail.
  • Create, document, and share effective outreach sequences and best practices with the broader sales team.

Meeting Booking & CRM Excellence

  • Meet or exceed monthly and quarterly targets for booked and attended discovery meetings.
  • Maintain weekly activity benchmarks across calls, emails, and sequence completion.
  • Ensure best-in-class CRM hygiene, including accurate activity tracking, pipeline stages, and contact data.

Conference & Campaign Support

  • Drive pre- and post-conference execution, including list uploads, lead sheets, and AE briefings.
  • Provide Account Executives with relevant prospect intelligence, including state-specific context and lead status.
  • Execute timely, strategic post-event follow-up and integrate learnings into ongoing campaigns.

Ideal Candidate Profile:

  • Enterpriser: A proactive self-starter with ownership mentality and bias toward action.
  • High Sense of Urgency: Operates quickly without sacrificing accuracy or quality.
  • Detail-Oriented Operator: Maintains high standards for research, execution, and CRM hygiene.
  • Adaptable & Flexible: Comfortable pivoting tactics as strategies evolve.
  • Persistent & Tenacious: Demonstrates grit and resilience in outbound prospecting.
  • Customer-Centric Thinker: Seeks to understand district needs and align value accordingly.
  • Strong Communicator: Clear, concise written and verbal communicator.
  • Creative Problem Solver: Finds new and effective ways to engage prospects.
  • Self-Leader: Manages time, priorities, and goals with minimal oversight.

Requirements:

  • 1–3 years of experience in sales development, market development, or outbound prospecting (SaaS or EdTech preferred).
  • Experience working in a CRM environment (HubSpot strongly preferred).
  • Strong research, organizational, and time-management skills.
  • Comfort with high-volume outbound activity and performance-based goals.
  • Familiarity with the K–12 education market is a plus but not required.

Benefits:

  • Unlimited Paid Time Off
  • Flextime Options
  • Remote Work Options
  • Paid Holidays
  • Employee Stock Options
  • Paid Parental and Family Medical Leave
  • Full Employee Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • 401(k) Plan

Givebacks is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
